owner: CC owns the mechanism. Akien owns the design choice of what the fingerprint covers (record only, or record plus referenced artifacts).
intention: A gate crossing produces a cryptographic certificate — a sha256 over the crossing record's canonical JSON — so passage is provable and tamper-evident after the fact without re-running the gate or trusting only the git history.
why: The crossing record in history.json is the record of truth for gate passage (Law 7). Today it is a plain JSON object — editable in place with nothing noticing until the next git diff or build_inspector run. A fingerprint makes the record self-verifying: the hash travels with the record, and a verifier re-hashes to check. Two things git alone does not give: (1) in-place-edit detection before commit, (2) portable verification from the record alone without git history.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the certificate is the receipt that Law 8 was satisfied at a specific crossing.
Law 7 — errors are loud and permanent in records of truth; a fingerprinted crossing record cannot be silently edited.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics; the fingerprint makes tamper-evidence structural rather than relying on git discipline.

how.mechanism: After emit() builds the crossing record dict (transitions.py:1582-1638) and before projector.append_entry writes it, compute sha256 over the record's canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ': '), ensure_ascii=False — the same arguments source_fingerprint uses in validation_store.py). Append the hash as a 'fingerprint' field on the record itself.
how.verification: A verify_crossing_fingerprint() function in transitions.py re-serializes the record (minus the fingerprint field) and re-hashes. A build_inspector sieve runs this over all history.json files at each PROVEME crossing.
how.extends_existing_pattern: source_fingerprint in validation_store (sha256 over proof source files) is the existing pattern — same mechanism (hash for integrity), different subject (proof code vs crossing record). The two could chain: a crossing fingerprint that includes the proof's source_fingerprint links the attestations.

gates: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: the tester runs proof teeth — a fingerprinted record verifies, a tampered record does not, a record without a fingerprint is flagged. FEEDS BACK: a red routes to the builder with the tampered field and both hashes.
falsifier: DONE when every emit() crossing carries a fingerprint field verifiable by re-hashing, and an in-place edit of the record changes the hash. WRONG INTENT if the fingerprint requires re-running the gate (re-derivation, not a certificate), if nothing ever verifies it (ceremony — a hash nobody checks is a hash nobody has), or if it duplicates what git's own content-addressable storage already guarantees without adding portability or in-place-edit detection.
horizon: Small code change — a few lines in emit() after the record dict is built, plus a matching verifier and sieve. Bounded build.
dependencies: cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit — the chokepoint where the fingerprint is computed.
distinctions_recorded: FINGERPRINT vs GIT INTEGRITY: git's content-addressable storage provides integrity for committed files. The fingerprint adds in-place-edit detection BEFORE commit and portable verification from the record alone.

FINGERPRINT vs SOURCE_FINGERPRINT: source_fingerprint covers proof source code (has the proof changed since sealed?). This covers crossing records (was the crossing record tampered with after the crossing?). Different subjects, same mechanism.
FINGERPRINT vs STATE-AND-HISTORY-DOOR: that ticket catches in-place edits via git-diff; this catches them via hash mismatch. Different detection mechanisms, complementary.
provenance: Born from idea 2026-08-28-fingerprint-gates-issue-certificates-of-passage (Akien: 'gates issue certificates of passage... Maybe a crypto fingerprint thing?'). Ticketed 2026-08-29.

watchme.trigger: after the first 50 crossings that carry fingerprints — enough traffic to see whether anyone verifies
watchme.enough: when at least one verification has run against a live crossing (not a test fixture) and the fingerprint caught at least one real tampered record OR the watch has seen 200 crossings with zero verification failures
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the verification count, the tampering count, and the proportion verified
watchme.consumer: the trouble lane on a verification failure
